haiku-low.q1: After step 2's database transaction commits. The ack carries msg_id and seq, and does not wait for recipients.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error. Nothing commits, so no outbox row and no fan-out. Retry must reuse the same client_msg_id; the unique (sender, client_msg_id) key prevents a second row.
haiku-low.q3: When its heartbeats stop for 30 seconds. The presence entry's 30-second TTL then expires, and the user counts as offline.
haiku-low.q4: Its pending row stays. The sweeper sends one push 5 seconds after hinted_at, if still unacked. A late duplicate is dropped by msg_id.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is logged and never retried. push_sent_at is still set, and the pending row is untouched, so sync can still deliver the message.
haiku-low.q6: In sequence order: pending rows joined with messages, ordered by conv_id and seq, in pages of 100. The client drops duplicates by msg_id.
haiku-low.q7: The message and outbox row commit together. The unpublished outbox row survives a crash, and a later relay tick publishes it to the topic.
haiku-low.q8: In the presence key-value store, one key per user with a 30-second TTL. Entries lapse unless heartbeats refresh them, which removes a dead connection's entry.
haiku-low.q9: Fan-out worker calls the presence node, which passes the full hint over the open WebSocket. The client's ack of msg_id confirms arrival and deletes the pending row.
haiku-low.q10: In the pending table in the Message Store, written by the fan-out worker at step 5, not the send transaction. A row is deleted on client ack or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The user's pending rows joined with messages, ordered by conv_id and seq, read in pages of 100 after presence is written.
haiku-low.q12: Unacked topic message is redelivered by the broker. Steps 5 to 8 are safe to repeat, so ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and push guards prevent duplicate effects.

sonnet.q1: After the single database transaction (step 2) commits, and only then; it never waits for recipients. The ack carries {msg_id, seq}.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error instead of an ack. Nothing commits, so there is no outbox row and nobody receives the message. The retry must carry the same client_msg_id (with the same sender); the unique (sender, client_msg_id) key keeps at most one row.
sonnet.q3: After no heartbeat for 30 seconds (presence TTL of 30 s; heartbeats are sent every 10 s), the user counts as offline.
sonnet.q4: The pending row is still there, so the sweeper (hinted_at older than 5 s, push_sent_at NULL) claims it and sends a push (once, best effort). The message may later arrive again via sync, and duplicates are dropped by msg_id.
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged and the push is never retried. push_sent_at is already set, and the pending row is untouched, so storage is unaffected. The recipient still gets the message through sync on reconnect.
sonnet.q6: In sequence order: sync reads pending rows joined with messages ordered by conv_id and seq, in pages of 100, then sends a sync-complete frame. The client drops duplicates by msg_id and orders each conversation by seq, and acks each message.
sonnet.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message, so it is committed with it. The relay (separate process) publishes unpublished outbox rows on a 500 ms timer, so a later tick publishes it even if the gateway crashed. The durable topic then holds it until a consumer acks, and fan-out is idempotent.
sonnet.q8: In Presence: a separate key-value store (not the Message Store), one key per user holding gateway node address and connection id, non-durable. Each entry has a 30-second TTL and expires on its own if heartbeats stop refreshing it.
sonnet.q9: The fan-out worker looks up the node address in presence and sends a hint with the full message through an internal call to that gateway node; the node passes it over the recipient's WebSocket if it has an open socket for that connection id. The client's ack {msg_id} confirms arrival, and it deletes the pending row.
sonnet.q10: In the pending table in the Message Store. It is written by the fan-out worker at step 5 (one row per recipient, batch insert, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), not by the send transaction. A row is deleted when the client acks the msg_id, or by the sweeper when it passes expires_at (created_at + 30 days).
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads the user's pending rows joined with messages, ordered by conv_id and seq, in pages of 100 (after first writing presence). The client fetches any remaining gaps, such as messages that expired from pending, from the conversation history API.
sonnet.q12: The topic message was not acked, so the broker redelivers it. Steps 5 to 8 are idempotent and safe to repeat: pending inserts use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, hinted_at and push_sent_at are set only if NULL (at most one push per row). Recipients already handled are not duplicated, and the rest are processed.
